speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Education in each year for the past five years, what is the respective breakdown on the median and average ratio of full-time trained and untrained school counsellors to students in primary schools and secondary schools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Prior to their formal training at the National Institute of Education, untrained school counsellors are attached to schools to learn from experienced school counsellors but will not be involved in actual counselling work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Beside school counsellors, students are also supported by a network of teacher-counsellors, flexi-adjunct school counsellors, peer supporters and community resources such as Response, Early Assessment and Intervention for Community Mental Health teams and Family Service Centres.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And I thank the Minister of State for the reply.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have seen the good and important work our school counsellors do, but I think they need some help, they are severely understaffed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I ask the Minister of State whether we are planning to increase the number of trained school counsellors in school?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What is the ideal number and perhaps what is the timeframe for this increase?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Hon Member Louis Ng has mentioned that this might not be a sufficient number.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Actually, our schools can also engage flexi-adjunct school counsellors to supplement their short-term manpower needs and this is at the discretion of the school leaders and management.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: I hope the hon Member and Members in this Chamber take a more holistic approach towards supporting students with counselling needs.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: The load cannot fall fully on the school counsellors.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Instead, we need to look wider at the community support within the school – fellow students, teachers, adjunct school counsellors and outside of the schools, the community partners.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Our interest must be to provide adequate and effective support to our students.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: We talked about the teacher-counsellors, but I think we agreed that teachers are really quite overworked.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I just spent the weekend with the Singapore Teachers' Union talking about the workload and their concerns.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Now you are asking to do counselling work as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: And that is why the clarification really is on whether we can increase the support to school counsellors, separate from teacher-counsellors, so teachers can focus on teaching and school counsellors can help the students who really do need that help quite desperately.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We recognise that counselling work is demanding and teacher-counsellors have to balance their teaching and counselling workload.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: And training for teacher-counsellors also has been enhanced to equip them not only to support their students' well-being, but also better manage their own well-being.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We do that for the school counsellors too.
